scope: Next independent F2/C native SLA signal gap; review before changing shared customer/health code
facts: Customer360.overview currently counts distinct ticket IDs by running/paused clock due_at alone.
ClockProjection uses native elapsed business time, the immutable calendar snapshot and budget; a stored deadline crossing a weekend does not by itself prove a breach.
CustomerSignals consumes Customer360 sla_breached in health, priority and automatic ticket actions.
AttendanceMetrics separately intersects native customer-view and SLA-view ticket scopes and calls ClockBreachQuery.
Customer360 currently checks native tickets/customers access for this count but has no distinct SLA-view capability in its summary.
SnapshotAccess currently reauthorizes source IDs and known module capabilities; distinct SLA capability/clock evidence is not represented in CustomerSignals.SOURCE_MANIFEST.
implementation_constraints: Reuse native policy scopes and ClockProjection; no deadline-only breach heuristic or invented SLA formula.
Do not change calendars, current clocks, immutable snapshots, role grants or old versions.
Unavailable SLA permission must not become a fabricated zero or healthy observation.
Current customer/health derived numeric SLA facts and their cached sources must remain authorized after revocation.
Keep critical-ticket visibility and existing native editing/transfers; no blanket analyst removal or role mutation.
Test distinct affected-ticket counts, paused and weekend boundary cases, module/unit/supervision/tenant denial and historical immutability.
status: Native implementation and directed regressions passed; no stage/visual closure.
